**2026-10-29.** A patch release: a lost-message fix, a boot failure under file-descriptor pressure,
and less CPU per step. Everything in the v0.6.0 release notes applies. Durability is unchanged —
no commit was added, removed or made asynchronous. The snapshot format and the database schema are
unchanged, so an instance parked by a 0.6.5 engine resumes under 0.6.6, and there is no migration.
The `q:` namespace is untouched.

## Fixed

**A local answer that reached its target before the target parked was lost.** Since 0.6.5 a
`local://` delivery goes out the moment the sender's step commits. A process that sends a request
at one park and reaches the wait for the answer one step later (a `q:reply continue="true"`, a
timer, any other wait in between) could get the answer before it parked there. The engine refused
it — no live instance carries the wait's alias (`SUTRA.RUNTIME.RELAY.CORRELATION_NOT_FOUND`), or the
instance is parked elsewhere (`SUTRA.RUNTIME.RESUME.NOT_WAITING`) or not suspended — and the
in-process sink took the refusal as permanent, so the delivery waited five minutes at the poison
horizon. These refusals are now marked `sutra.waitPending=true`. The local sink offers such a
delivery again after 5 to 80 ms (155 ms in all), then retries it with the outbox backoff for up to
8 attempts (about four minutes); after that it takes the usual poison posture — kept with its last
error, redelivered at the horizon. Nothing is lost either way. A finished instance is never
wait-pending, and other transports keep their own handling. The conformance test `tc_wait_race`
(a send, a two-second timer, then the wait) lost all 20 answers on 0.6.5 and settles all 20, once
each, on 0.6.6.

**An HTTP client build could panic a lane when file descriptors ran out.** Each outbound HTTP
client — one per execution lane for inline calls, plus each sink — read the platform CA bundle when
it was built; under `EMFILE` the build panicked ("native TLS root store") and the lane's deliveries
were dead-lettered. The bundle is now read once per process and every client starts from that
configuration (`sutra_channels::shared_client_tls_config`). A failed first read is not remembered.

## Changed: less CPU per step

- A pooled database connection is pinged before use only after a second idle; it is still pinged
  when it is returned, and closed if that fails.
- `BEGIN` and the deployment-scope `set_config` are one query: one round trip less per transaction.
- A stored instance is parsed once per load instead of two or three times.
- FEEL expressions, `matches()` patterns and SRL rulesets are parsed or compiled once per thread
  instead of per evaluation (pure functions of their text; failures are never cached; bounded).
- The outbox dispatcher's memory of recently delivered rows expires in time order instead of
  rescanning itself on every batch.
- The XSD validator counts columns incrementally; it was quadratic on a one-line document.

Measured on one 12-core laptop with durable PostgreSQL:

| workload | build | completions/s | p50 | p99 | CPU per completion |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| relay (`tools/sutra-load-test`), 500/s | 0.6.5 | 499.1 | 27 ms | 75 ms | 8.05 ms (engine + PostgreSQL) |
| relay, 500/s | 0.6.6 | 499.1 | 25 ms | 75 ms | 6.33 ms |
| an XML-heavy downstream workload, 500/s offered | 0.6.5 | 372.1 | 13.6 s | 22.4 s | 21.6 ms (engine) |
| the same, 500/s offered | 0.6.6 | 410.8 | 8.8 s | 16.2 s | 18.6 ms |

WAL flushes per completion are unchanged. `tools/sutra-load-test/relay-bench.sh` now also reports
PostgreSQL CPU and CPU milliseconds per completion.

## Upgrading

Nothing to do. A distribution that builds its own HTTPS clients can start from
`sutra_channels::shared_client_tls_config()` instead of reading the native roots itself.

## Install

```bash
docker pull ghcr.io/startr-trade/sutra:0.6.6
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/startr-trade/sutra/main/scripts/install.sh | sh -s -- --version v0.6.6
```

The library crates are on crates.io as `sutra-feel = "0.6.6"` and `sutra-dmn = "0.6.6"`.
